newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures slip back as sterling firms.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures slip back as sterling firms.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures slipped back from Tuesday's advance as the market adjusted lower on sterling's renewed strength against the dollar, traders said.
But the losses were slim and traders said the market was likely to extend current consolidation from last week's decline.
By the morning finish, May was four stg down at 876 stg a tonne. Overall volume was a thin 1,110 lots.
Traders said there was talk of renewed origin hedge sales notably from Ghana and Ivory Coast.
This was met with less aggressive buying from manufacturers.

Faced with little fundamental and technical impetus, cocoa is likely to remain trapped in the current downward trend. But the mood could change if May rallies back above the 900 stg level, traders said.
They were keeping a close watch on the first notice day for the spot March contract.
But with a reasonable amount of cocoa being graded, they did not anticipate a supply problem in meeting physical delivery. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
